title: Does it have this member?
description:
Before concepts, the way to ask "does type `T` have a member function `toString()`?" was the *detection idiom*, built on SFINAE and `std::void_t`. You will meet it in older code, so write it once by hand.

Complete `HasToString<T>` so that it derives from `std::true_type` when `std::declval<T>().toString()` is a valid expression, and from `std::false_type` otherwise.

The primary template (already written) is the "no" answer. Add a partial specialization that is only viable when the expression compiles.
hints: The specialization's extra template argument is `std::void_t<decltype(std::declval<T>().toString())>`. When the expression does not compile, that specialization silently drops out and the primary (false) one is used.
